Supply-chain hardening for `package:boring`'s CI. None of it depends on how the prebuilt libraries are distributed. This is the first PR in a stack; #2866 (bundling the libraries in the published package) builds on it.

- **NASM:** replaces `ilammy/setup-nasm`, which downloads NASM from a mutable branch of its repository without checking the download, with a local composite action, `.github/actions/setup-nasm`. It downloads NASM 2.16.01 directly from nasm.us and verifies a pinned SHA-256 (matching Scoop's manifest). It's used in `boring.yaml` and in `boring_binaries.yaml`, which builds the released Windows libraries.
- **macOS Linux cross-toolchain:** replaces the unpinnable `brew install messense/macos-cross-toolchains/...` tap in the `test` job of `boring.yaml` with a direct download of the `v15.2.0` release tarball (arm64/x86_64) and a SHA-256 check, like the Windows cross-toolchain.
- **`precompile` permissions:** `precompile` runs compilers and other build tools, so it no longer gets `id-token: write` / `attestations: write`. A new `attest` job, which only downloads the `binaries-*` artifacts, attests their provenance before `release` uploads them. `gh attestation verify <file> --repo dart-lang/tools` keeps working.

+name: Set up NASM
+description: >-
+  Installs NASM on Windows, which assembles the x86-64 assembly of the BoringSSL
+  that pkgs/boring vendors. Downloads the release from nasm.us and checks it
+  against a pinned SHA-256, instead of trusting a third-party action and its
+  mirror.
+
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Install NASM
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        NASM_VERSION: 2.16.01
+        # nasm.us doesn't publish checksums. This is the SHA-256 of
+        # nasm-2.16.01-win64.zip from nasm.us, which matches the hash in Scoop's
+        # manifest of NASM 2.16.01.
+        NASM_SHA256: 029eed31faf0d2c5f95783294432cbea6c15bf633430f254bb3c1f195c67ca3a
+      run: |
+        url="https://www.nasm.us/pub/nasm/releasebuilds/$NASM_VERSION/win64/nasm-$NASM_VERSION-win64.zip"
+        curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" "$url"
+        actual="$(sha256sum < "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
+        if [ "$actual" != "$NASM_SHA256" ]; then
+          echo "::error::Expected SHA-256 $NASM_SHA256 for $url, got $actual."
+          exit 1
+        fi
+        7z x "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" -o"$RUNNER_TEMP" -y > /dev/null
+        "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm-$NASM_VERSION/nasm.exe" -v
+        cygpath -w "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm-$NASM_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

> [!NOTE]
> This PR was generated by an AI coding agent (Jetski) on behalf of @mosuem.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Stacked on #2899 (this PR targets its branch, so the diff only shows the bundling change).

Bundles `package:boring`'s prebuilt libraries in the package archive published to pub.dev, instead of attaching them to `boring-binaries-*` GitHub releases that the build hook downloads, and publishes with SLSA Build L3 provenance via `dart-lang/setup-dart/.github/workflows/publish.yml` (dart-lang/setup-dart#213).

**CI**
- `boring_binaries.yaml` now also runs on `boring-v<version>` tags. It builds the libraries for all 11 prebuilt targets from the tagged commit (`bundled-files-*`), tests the archive on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and delegates publishing to `dart-lang/setup-dart/.github/workflows/publish.yml` (`bundled-files`, `attest: true`, running in `test-run` mode on non-tag runs). `publish.yaml` skips `boring-v*` tags so firehose does not publish the package without the libraries.
- Drops per-binary intermediate provenance attestation in favor of `setup-dart`'s SLSA Build L3 attestation over the complete `package.tar.gz` archive (which covers all bundled libraries).
- Removes the `release` and `pin` jobs, so there are no more `boring-binaries-*` pre-releases or pin PRs. The libraries are built from the tagged commit, so they always match the vendored BoringSSL. That makes `hashes.dart`, `tool/regenerate_hashes.dart`, `tool/check_prebuilt_binaries.sh`, and the matching steps in `boring.yaml` unnecessary.
- Adds `pkgs/boring/.pubignore`, which pub reads instead of `.gitignore`, so `prebuilt/` goes into the archive while git still ignores it.
- Supply-chain hardening (pinned NASM, pinned macOS cross-toolchain, `precompile` without OIDC permissions) is split out into #2899, which this PR is stacked on. The pinned macOS cross-toolchain step moves with the cross-compilation tests into `boring_binaries.yaml`, and the separate `attest` job is dropped since `setup-dart` attests the whole archive.

**Build hook**
- `fetch` mode (`hook/build.dart`) and the link-failure fallback (`hook/link.dart`) now read `prebuilt/<target>/<library>` from the package root (`lib/src/hook_helpers/prebuilt.dart`, which replaces `fetch.dart`). There's no download, hash check, or cache anymore.
- A git/path dependency has no `prebuilt/`, so it gets a `BuildError` that points to `buildMode: checkout`.
- `tool/precompile_binaries.dart` writes to `prebuilt/<target>/` instead of `bin/boring-<target>-<library>`. A local run therefore makes a checkout usable in `fetch` mode.

**Tests**
- Moves the cross-compilation tests from `tree_shaking_test.dart` to `prebuilt_test.dart`. They now build against `BORING_PACKAGE_DIR` (the extracted archive), and the file also checks that all 22 libraries are there. Without that variable the file is skipped, as it is in `boring.yaml`. The cross-toolchain setup moves to `boring_binaries.yaml` with it.

**CI notes**
- The archive test on Ubuntu currently fails on the Dart executable's ELF `e_machine` check due to a Dart 3.14.0 `dart build cli` Linux cross-compilation launcher regression (see dart-lang/sdk#64915; WIP SDK fix at https://dart-review.googlesource.com/c/sdk/+/577541).
- `publish` is temporarily pinned to `dart-lang/setup-dart#213` (`publish-bundled-files`, stacked on `#212` and `#210`); repin to `main` / `@v1` once those land.

**Notes**
- Keep the existing `boring-binaries-*` releases: published versions ? 0.4.2 still download from them.
- `fetch` keeps its name so existing `user_defines` don't break. Renaming it (e.g. to `prebuilt`, with `fetch` as an alias) could be a follow-up.
- Overlaps with #2773, whose `publish_boring.yaml` is superseded by the `setup-dart` call in `boring_binaries.yaml`, and supersedes #2782, since there are no more pin PRs.

[boring] Pin NASM and the macOS cross-toolchain, and attest in a separate job

- ilammy/setup-nasm downloads NASM from a mutable branch of its repository,
  and only then from nasm.us, without checking the download, so its pinned
  commit doesn't pin the NASM that assembles the released Windows libraries.
  A local composite action, .github/actions/setup-nasm, downloads NASM
  2.16.01 from nasm.us instead and checks it against a pinned SHA-256.
- The `test` job of boring.yaml installed the macOS Linux cross-toolchain
  from a Homebrew tap, which can't be pinned. It now downloads the v15.2.0
  release tarball and checks its SHA-256, like the Windows cross-toolchain.

  attest the libraries, so every step in it, including compilers and
  third-party actions, could mint OIDC tokens. A new `attest` job downloads
  the libraries and attests them, and `precompile` only gets
  `contents: read`.

Avoids any text-mode stdin handling on Windows.

[boring] Hash the downloads via stdin again

path such as D:\a\_temp and prefixes its output with `\`, so the hash
didn't match.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Avoid redirecting binary files to `stdin` using `<` on Windows, as some environments or tool configurations can default to text mode for `stdin`, potentially leading to CRLF translation or premature EOF (e.g., if the binary contains `0x1A`). Passing the file path directly to `sha256sum` is safer and more robust.

```yaml
        actual="$(sha256sum "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```
Done in 699f4cd9e, also for the two cross-toolchain checks in `boring.yaml`.

Reverted in 3a43ff46d: with a path argument, GNU `sha256sum` escapes the backslashes of the Windows `$RUNNER_TEMP` (`D:\a\_temp`) and prefixes the hash with `\`, which failed the check. Git Bash reads stdin in binary mode, so `< file` is fine here.

timeline.message:
[boring] Pin NASM and the macOS cross-toolchain, and attest in a separate job

- ilammy/setup-nasm downloads NASM from a mutable branch of its repository,
  and only then from nasm.us, without checking the download, so its pinned
  commit doesn't pin the NASM that assembles the released Windows libraries.
  A local composite action, .github/actions/setup-nasm, downloads NASM
  2.16.01 from nasm.us instead and checks it against a pinned SHA-256.
- The `test` job of boring.yaml installed the macOS Linux cross-toolchain
  from a Homebrew tap, which can't be pinned. It now downloads the v15.2.0
  release tarball and checks its SHA-256, like the Windows cross-toolchain.
- The `precompile` job had `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` to
  attest the libraries, so every step in it, including compilers and
  third-party actions, could mint OIDC tokens. A new `attest` job downloads
  the libraries and attests them, and `precompile` only gets
  `contents: read`.

Avoid redirecting binary files to `stdin` using `<` on Windows, as some environments or tool configurations can default to text mode for `stdin`, potentially leading to CRLF translation or premature EOF (e.g., if the binary contains `0x1A`). Passing the file path directly to `sha256sum` is safer and more robust.

```yaml
        actual="$(sha256sum "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```

+name: Set up NASM
+description: >-
+  Installs NASM on Windows, which assembles the x86-64 assembly of the BoringSSL
+  that pkgs/boring vendors. Downloads the release from nasm.us and checks it
+  against a pinned SHA-256, instead of trusting a third-party action and its
+  mirror.
+
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Install NASM
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        NASM_VERSION: 2.16.01
+        # nasm.us doesn't publish checksums. This is the SHA-256 of
+        # nasm-2.16.01-win64.zip from nasm.us, which matches the hash in Scoop's
+        # manifest of NASM 2.16.01.
+        NASM_SHA256: 029eed31faf0d2c5f95783294432cbea6c15bf633430f254bb3c1f195c67ca3a
+      run: |
+        url="https://www.nasm.us/pub/nasm/releasebuilds/$NASM_VERSION/win64/nasm-$NASM_VERSION-win64.zip"
+        curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" "$url"
+        actual="$(sha256sum < "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

+  Installs NASM on Windows, which assembles the x86-64 assembly of the BoringSSL
+  that pkgs/boring vendors. Downloads the release from nasm.us and checks it
+  against a pinned SHA-256, instead of trusting a third-party action and its
+  mirror.
+
+runs:
+  using: composite
+  steps:
+    - name: Install NASM
+      shell: bash
+      env:
+        NASM_VERSION: 2.16.01
+        # nasm.us doesn't publish checksums. This is the SHA-256 of
+        # nasm-2.16.01-win64.zip from nasm.us, which matches the hash in Scoop's
+        # manifest of NASM 2.16.01.
+        NASM_SHA256: 029eed31faf0d2c5f95783294432cbea6c15bf633430f254bb3c1f195c67ca3a
+      run: |
+        url="https://www.nasm.us/pub/nasm/releasebuilds/$NASM_VERSION/win64/nasm-$NASM_VERSION-win64.zip"
+        curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" "$url"
+        actual="$(sha256sum < "$RUNNER_TEMP/nasm.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
